summary: Sras Rinpoche III is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Thubten Kunga, at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1971), and at Gyume Tantric Monastery (1971). He held posts at Rizong, Drepung Loseling (1984), and Gyume Tantric Monastery (1995–2008).

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Sravana Borkataky-Varma studied at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016). She held teaching posts at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington (~2017–2021), a fellowship at Harvard (~2020–2021), and taught at the University of Houston (~2021).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University (~1957–1961), and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966). He served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1977 to 1997.

Sri Anirvan (1896–1978) worked in Indology and philosophy. He completed his studies at the University of Dhaka (~1914–1916), Sanskrit College and University (~1916–1918), and the University of Calcutta.

Srikanth Kaul worked in Indology and history/archaeology. In 1967, he was attested holding posts at Government Degree College, Sopore, and as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.

Srinivas H. Ritti (1928–2021) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as an Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964) and Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and as Professor at Karnatak University (attested 1975).

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1962–1967). He subsequently served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Rang Mahal School and Government College University, Lahore (BA 1881). He served as Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1883), founded Panini Office (1891), and was a Fellow at Allahabad.

Stacey Van Vleet is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Colorado, Columbia University (PhD attested 2006), and under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, later holding a post at Columbia (attested 2013).

Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served with the East India Company (~1795–1824), founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, and became its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a Sinologist and scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and held posts at Collège de France (from 1821; Chair of Chinese 1832–1873), Bibliothèque nationale, and INALCO (1863–1871).

Stanislav Grof is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Prague (~1950–1956). He held posts at Czech psychiatric institutions, Johns Hopkins (1967–1969), Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969–1973), Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and CIIS (1994–2015).

Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. In 1922 he founded and served as professor at the University of Warsaw, and was later a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Stanley Abe is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held an academic post at Duke University, where he was attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Cecil Sutton (1907–1993) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and at the India Office Library (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Columbia, Tübingen under Paul Thieme, and Yale (PhD ~1957–1963). He served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (~1976–2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Ceylon and Cornell (PhD ~1951–1954). He held posts at the University of Ceylon (1955–1960), Cambridge (1963–1973), Chicago (1973–1976), and Harvard (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Loyola University New Orleans (~1961–1965), Tulane University (~1966–1968), and the University of Texas at Austin (~1968–1972), and held a post at the University of Kansas (~1976–2014).

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard (PhD ~1962–1966) under Masatoshi Nagatomi, Kodo Sawaki, and Gyokusen Hosaka. He held posts at Komazawa, SOAS, and Yale (emeritus 1968).

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at City College of New York (BA ~1949–1953) and the University of Pennsylvania (MA ~1953–1955). He spent his academic career at UCLA from 1959 to 2002.
